transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 min (recording)
Attendees: Lina Torres (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Emma Patel (EchoHealth SRE), Rajiv Nair (EchoHealth CTO), Tom Weller (Product), Priya Shah (Security)
---
00:00 Lina (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro round, I'm Lina, AE at Redwood, and Marcus here is our SE.
00:07 Marcus (Redwood SE): Hi all, Marcus. I'll be driving the console walkthrough and the request forensics demo today.
00:12 Rajiv (EchoHealth): Rajiv, CTO. We have some folks from SRE and security with us. We're hoping to understand how Redwood helps us debug and do postmortems, especially for PII-safe playback.
00:23 Emma (EchoHealth): Emma, SRE. We get a lot of alerts that are noisy and want faster triage, and we need to know what user data touched the request.
00:32 Lina: Great. Agenda: quick qualification — current infra and constraints, then a live Console demo: tracing, request inspector, playback, KV/ cache fallbacks and error analysis playbook. Then time for Q&A and next steps.
00:50 Tom (EchoHealth): Sounds good. Quick FYI, we're on Kubernetes EKS in us-west-2, using a mix of OpenAI API now and some self-hosted models. Latency targets are 150ms p50 for interactive UX. Cost is a concern, we want to avoid overpaying for every token when we can.
01:08 Marcus: Cool, that matches a lot of customers. A couple quick qual questions: do you plan dedicated capacity or hosted? And what's your data residency / encryption posture?
01:18 Priya (Security): We need SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML with SCIM, and KMS integration. If possible, private deployment in our VPC for PHI datasets.
01:28 Lina: Noted. We support hosted for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for predictability, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need air-gapped. KMS and audit logs are part of the Private package.
01:38 Marcus: Ok jumping into the demo. I'll share my screen. Loading Console -> Requests -> Inspector.
01:46 Marcus: First thing we look at is the request timeline view. Here you can see individual requests, latency buckets, and an error heatmap. For this tenant I'm filtering to a trace ID created from a sample health-check flow.
02:03 Marcus: You can expand a request and see the full request/response payload, but note we mask PII by default in hosted if you toggle the masking setting — in dedicated/private you can manage masking rules and KMS-wrapped tokenization.
02:18 Emma: Can you show how masking looks? We need to guarantee PHI isn't stored in plaintext.
02:24 Marcus: Sure. Toggle on PII redaction — you can see names, SSNs, and PHI fields are replaced. Under private mode, we support in-flight encryption and you'll see a flag that payloads were stored with customer KMS. In hosted mode we still keep audit logs but we recommend dedicated if you need deterministic key control.
02:44 Marcus: Now drill into an error event. See this error spike at 14:32? Expand it. You get the error stack, model variant, exact prompt tokens, and a sketch of the model kernel used. Occasionally the ASR transcription in these logs messes up model name — like it shows redwood-lm-v2 as redwood-lm-v too, transcription artifact.
03:05 Rajiv: How do we link that to application logs? We have correlation IDs in our app logs but not always attached to model requests.
03:12 Marcus: Great question. Redwood injects a request_id header and we surface trace context (trace_id/span_id) that you can propagate through your app. On the timeline you can click 'Linked logs' which shows your app logs tied by correlation id. We can also ingest your existing logs via a secure forwarder or CloudWatch integration.
03:30 Marcus: I'll open Request Playback next. This is important for reproducible root cause analysis. The playback replays the exact token sequence and model variant used, including KV cache state. For privacy, when you request a playback where payloads contain PHI, playback runs in a private sandbox or in your VPC.
03:58 Emma: The KV cache part — sometimes we get flakey responses due to cache invalidation. How does Redwood show cache hits/misses?
04:06 Marcus: Good — in the request details we show a 'KV cache snapshot' with hit/miss markers per token range. We annotate fallback behaviors e.g., if the request fell back to a smaller quantized model for cost reasons. Sometimes transcriptions show that as 'K V cash fallback' — ignore that, that's just the ASR.
04:26 Marcus: Here's a real example: request A had a partial KV miss at token 128 and paged to the next chunk, which added 50ms. The timeline shows the exact step where kernel selection happened.
04:39 Tom: Can the playback be run against our private deploy? We need to ensure it doesn't leave our VPC.
04:45 Marcus: Yes. For Private/Dedicated we can run playback entirely within your VPC. For hosted we provide an ephemeral isolated environment with strict retention and redact options.
04:55 Priya: Audit logs and RBAC — who can run playback? We need separation of duties.
05:01 Marcus: Console integrates with SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning. Each action has an audit trail entry. You can define RBAC roles so only particular groups can run playback or view raw payload. We also have an approval workflow if you want a two-step approval for sensitive replays.
05:18 Rajiv: Latency vs cost tradeoffs — earlier you mentioned fallback to quantized models. How is that surfaced?
05:25 Marcus: We tag requests with the runtime profile: model version, quantization profile, kernel set, GPU type. If a request is routed to a cost-optimized variant we mark it 'fallback: quantized-ggml' or similar. The request timeline will show the delta in latency and token cost impact per request.
05:41 Marcus: Now I'll demo tracing across distributed services. I trigger a synthetic failing flow. You can see the trace waterfall and the span where Redwood's model inference occurred. Under the span you can expand subcalls and the exact prompt used.
06:00 Marcus: We also provide a lightweight trace correlation library — if you include our header or SDK snippet we auto-propagate trace IDs. No need to change much in your app.
06:12 Emma: Regarding retention, how long are full payloads kept? We're sensitive because of PHI.
06:18 Lina: By default hosted has 30 days full payload retention, logs longer. For Dedicated/Private you pick retention, and you can configure automatic deletion and customer-controlled key rotation. We can also set up short-lived retention for pilot tests.
06:29 Priya: Does Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
06:33 Marcus: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer HSM/KMS providers. We can store payloads encrypted with keys you manage.
06:40 Marcus: Ok switching to 'Error root cause playbook' in the Console. This is an opinionated flow we built: 1) Identify spike, 2) isolate representative request via sampling, 3) run Request Playback with KV snapshot, 4) check model variant and kernel selection, 5) check upstream app logs, 6) run differential prompt test. The Console has a guided checklist and auto-suggested test prompts.
07:05 Rajiv: Differential prompt test?
07:07 Marcus: Yes — you run the same prompt with and without certain context or inputs to see if the model behavior changes. We automate side-by-side comparison and flag token-level divergence.
07:20 Marcus: I'll show a side-by-side: original request vs sanitized request. You can diff the token outputs, see which token positions diverged and which model internals (attention patterns) changed — we surface a simple explanation like 'search context trimmed caused hallucination on token 23'.
07:36 Emma: How accurate are those explanations? We need to avoid overinterpreting heuristics in our postmortem.
07:42 Marcus: They're heuristics built from telemetry and kernel-level metrics, we label them as 'likely cause' and provide confidence. It's a starting point for your engineers; you still validate manually in the playback sandbox.
07:55 Marcus: Now I'll simulate an incident where the runtime fell back to a quantized path because of autoscaler pressure.
08:03 Marcus: Notice the autoscaler event tied to the span. The Console shows an autoscale window and a capacity event — that gives you the 'why' behind the latency spike. You can also link alerts from PagerDuty/Slack so runbooks are created automatically.
08:22 Tom: For the pilot we want to measure triage time improvement. Do you have suggested metrics?
08:28 Lina: Yep. Time-to-identify root cause, time-to-remediation, percentage of incidents resolved without escalating to infra, and reduction in mean-time-to-replay. We'll share suggested dashboards.
08:40 Emma: Can we export the Request Inspector data for our own postmortem storage? We want a permanent artifact in our incident tracker but PII redacted.
08:48 Marcus: You can export sanitized transcripts as JSON or attach a pointer to an encrypted artifact stored in your S3 (we can push to your bucket with server-side encryption).
08:58 Marcus: Quick demo of 'Search by model behavior' — you can search all requests that terminated with 'terminated-early' or 'fallback-mode' and group by user id or route.
09:12 Rajiv: How does Redwood handle multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated?
09:17 Lina: Dedicated pools provide tenant isolation at the workload level; you choose tenancy model. Private gives you full network isolation and your own control plane. Our dedicated tenants still have strong namespace isolation, RBAC, and audit.
09:30 Marcus: Ok switching to a small deep dive: kernel selection and profiling. Here we show kernel traces that indicate which GPU kernels were chosen and why. It helps SEs debug pathological tokenizations that cause kernel thrash.
09:44 Emma: That sounds very implementation level — useful for your SREs. Would our team need that level of access?
09:49 Marcus: Only if you opt-in. We surface summary-level kernel diagnostics for regular users and more granular traces for engineers with elevated access.
09:58 Marcus: We also have an automated 'roll-forward fallback' policy — if the primary model fails, the router can automatically send the request to a compatible variant, with a flag that indicates fallback reason. That is surfaced in the inspector so you can see the degraded output and choose to rollback.
10:18 Tom: Do you support canary and A/B in rollouts from the Console?
10:23 Marcus: Yes, you can run canary percentage, route by header, region, or customer tier. You can auto-promote or auto-rollback based on quality metrics tied to your eval sets.
10:35 Priya: Security question — can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
10:39 Marcus: Absolutely. We have native integrations with Splunk, Sumo Logic, Datadog, and you can forward JSON logs to your SIEM. Each audit entry includes actor, action, and request_id.
10:47 Rajiv: For the pilot we might want a private sandbox on our infra. How long to spin that up?
10:52 Lina: Typically 1-2 weeks for a Private sandbox with basic network and KMS integration. Dedicated sandbox is faster — a few days — depending on contract and capacity. We'll include provisioning timelines in the SOW.
11:05 Marcus: Jumping back to playback: I'll run a replay on a sampled problematic request. Running now.
11:08 Marcus: (typing) Replaying... we run the identical token stream against the same model variant. The Console shows token-by-token timings and we annotate when the KV cache is hit or misses. See at token 137 there's a long tail because we had to fetch replacement KV bucket from disk.
11:28 Emma: If we reproduce the issue, can the replay write to the same telemetry systems as production? We want to validate integrations.
11:33 Marcus: For Private we can replay against your upstream sinks. For hosted we can replay to a sandbox sink or to a scrubbed view — we don't recommend sending replays to live downstreams with PHI.
11:44 Tom: What's the support SLA for a pilot?
11:47 Lina: Pilot customers get priority support, 2 hour initial response for Sev 1s, and a dedicated CSM for onboarding. If you convert to Dedicated/Enterprise we can extend to SLA-backed commitments.
11:59 Marcus: Ok wrapping up demo portion. Quick Q&A.
12:02 Emma: Do you support field-level tokenization or redaction rules based on regex?
12:09 Marcus: Yes, we support regex-based scrubbing and tokenization libraries; rules are configurable per route. In Private, rules are enforced in your VPC so nothing leaves unencrypted.
12:20 Priya: For compliance audits, can we get a report of who viewed what during an incident?
12:25 Marcus: Yes — audit reports show views, replays, downloads with timestamps and actor. You can export them for audit purposes.
12:34 Rajiv: Any gotchas with our stack — EKS and mixture of OpenAI plus self-hosted models?
12:40 Marcus: You'll want to standardize correlation IDs across workloads so trace linking is reliable. We can provide a sidecar and SDK snippets for various languages. For mixed model fleets we'll suggest a routing policy that prefers your self-hosted model for sensitive data and falls back to hosted for non-sensitive lower-cost paths.
12:57 Tom: Cost question — how does playback cost get billed? Replay token charge or separate infra?
13:03 Lina: Playback compute is billed as replay compute; if it runs in your dedicated pool it's counted against reserved capacity. If it runs in hosted ephemeral we bill separately. We'll include estimates in the pilot pricing.
13:16 Marcus: Any final technical deep dives folks want?
13:20 Emma: One quick thing — can we attach our internal runbook to an alert so when the Console detects this particular error pattern it links out to our docs?
13:27 Marcus: Yes. You can attach runbooks or Jira playbooks and auto-create an incident with prefilled context.
13:36 Rajiv: Ok let's recap.
13:38 Lina: Recap: we showed Request Inspector, Request Playback, KV cache snapshots, kernel selection traces, RBAC/audit and private deployment options. Pilot asks: EchoHealth to provide sample logs and trace for a replay; Redwood to provide playbook deck, SOW and pilot pricing; provision sandbox.
13:56 Emma: I'll pull together sample logs and a representative trace by Tuesday.
14:00 Lina: Great. Marcus will send the playbook deck and the Console short demo clip. We'll aim to get the sandbox provisioned and SOW by next week.
14:10 Tom: One last note — we want the pilot to include measurements for triage time, number of replays before fix, and cost delta.
14:19 Lina: We'll include those metrics in the SOW.
14:24 Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll run internal stakeholder sync and get back with dates.
14:28 Marcus: Thanks all. I'll follow up with links: deck, sandbox quickstart, and a small script to forward CloudWatch logs.
14:35 Meeting end
